messages:
sophia_ml: Nightly eval alert — long-context harness shows a spike in early-termination for the new q4a-v2 quant build. Truncation and early-EOS are up across >16k sequences. Seen any more details?

ci-bot: nightly-eval/m-instruct-7b-q4a-v2 finished; failures 142 -> baseline 116; truncation regressions 37 (was 2). Report: https://ci.internal/reports/2281234567

dan_runtime: I pulled runtime metrics. We see wrap/stitch events clustered at token ~16384. Metric `ctx_window_ptr` reports wrap and `kv_stitch_mismatch` increments. No OOMs.

jordan_research: Repro locally with the eval harness and the converted q4a-v2 weights. Model often emits EOS and returns a short completion where SQL/instructions should continue. Not nondeterministic garbage, looks like an intentional EOS triggered by logits collapse.

mina_eval: Example (trimmed):
USER: "List migration steps and then output SQL to apply."
MODEL: "1. dump... 2. stop services 3. run migration
" <ends> — missing SQL block. Happens 60-75% for >16k prefixes.

alex_infra: Pulled a trace from a failing session:
TRACE: session=svc-c12 ctx_base=0x7ff4a offset=16128 len=512
KV-STITCH: expected_end=16640 actual_end=16384
WARN: prefix-anchor-mismatch anchor_seq=16128 read_back=0

dan_runtime: That read_back=0 is the red flag. The stitch code read an empty slot for the second half. We recently landed a kernel layout change in the q4a-v2 conversion that reorders cache entries for perf. Suspect index arithmetic mismatch between serializer and runtime accessors.

jordan_research: Also examined token logits at collapse: EOS probability spikes to ~0.9 instantly. KV read looks like zeros or repeated low-entropy vectors before collapse. Could be KV corruption or pointer misalignment.

mina_eval: Repro steps I used: 1) convert weights via q4a-v2 pipeline; 2) start mk-infer with --ctx-max=20000 --prefetch=on; 3) run failing prompt from nightly harness. Deterministic in my runs.

sophia_ml: Plan suggestions: 1) run canary with previous q4 kernel (rollback) to see if regressions disappear; 2) add KV fingerprinting at stitch points to compare across serialization boundaries; 3) try disabling prefetch to rule out timing/stitch order effects.

dan_runtime: I'll spin two canaries: one with old kernel layout, one with q4a-v2, both with KV fingerprint dump enabled. Also add a small KV-consistency checker that verifies prefix hash and slot contents on stitch.

alex_infra: Implemented a quick shim: dump fingerprint = sha1(prefix_slots) at every stitch. Pushing to canary images now.

jordan_research: Quick experiment: started service with --prefetch=off and continuous-batching=disabled. Early results: collapse rate drops ~80% on my local rig. That strongly implicates prefetch/stitch interaction.

ci-bot: note posted to #eng-ml-regressions; incident ticket created INC-228123.

mina_eval: Short-term mitigation: enforce ctx-max=16384 for pinned dedicated clusters to avoid wrapping. Will prepare rollout note for infra.

sophia_ml: Agreed, add guard to Dedicated config. If canary with old kernel passes and new kernel fails with fingerprints diverging, we can pin the regression to the q4a-v2 layout. If fingerprints match but logits diverge, then quant forward path likely unstable and we need bisect in conversion.

dan_runtime: ETA: canary runs + KV diffs within 2 hours. Will report back with fingerprint dumps attached.

sophia_ml: Thanks team — P0. Paste diffs here and tag me. :thumbsup:
